page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 32 vCPUs utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU.

The primary hardware accelerator configuration consists of two NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined total of 48 GB of VRAM. This server does not include any local storage, meaning storage resources must be provisioned and attached externally. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The shared CPU allocation presents a performance tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, non-burstable CPU processing, though the high memory density and dual NVIDIA L4 GPUs offer significant resource density for parallel processing. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that are heavily dependent on GPU acceleration and large memory footprints rather than dedicated single-core CPU performance. Appropriate workloads include machine learning inference, data science pipelines, and GPU-accelerated rendering.
